3. **The two brand wrappers duplicate each other.** `button`, `button-link`, `code-block`, `command-line`, `hero`, `icon`, `margin-note` and `view-toggle` exist in both `packages/orin` and `packages/twx`. The two `Button` files are the same size. Brand differences belong in tokens and recipe variants, not in a second component.
4. **The app layers build components with `css()`.** `apps/orin-dx` has about 40 component folders, 20 files calling `css()` or `cx()`, and 3 test files. `apps/techworx` has 12 files calling `css()`. These are design-system components living in the app, outside the recipe and test discipline.
5. **Enforcement does not exist.** `packages/rules` holds a README; the rules checker (SPEC-002) is not ported. The Playwright suites are not part of `just ci`, so layout, nav and print behaviour is checked only when someone runs them.
6. **Spacing is hand-placed.** About 170 margin declarations and 230 `gap`/`rowGap`/`columnGap` declarations across components and apps, and four uses of a layout primitive. There is no `Stack`, `Cluster` or `ButtonGroup` to own the space between siblings.

## Rule compliance

| Rule | Result |
| --- | --- |
| No `!important` | Source: none now (three were mine and are removed, `65abff2`). Generated CSS: one per app, all Panda's own `[hidden]` reset. |
| No `css()` in components | `packages/*`: 2 lines, both in Orin's `SiteViewToggle`. `apps/orin-dx`: 76 calls in 20 files. `apps/orin-dx-docs`: 12. `apps/techworx`: 78 in 12 files. |
| No inline style | `style=` in 15 places: Ledger, marks (`inkStyle`), `PageIntro` (the lattice span), `ThemeSwitch` (`--i`), `MenuSheet` (Ark's pointer-events), swatch and ladder data colours, one fixture. Data-driven custom properties are acceptable; the lattice span and the pointer-events override are not. |
| Semantic tokens only | Hex literals: techworx data (`_orin-dx-data.ts` 54, `marks.ts` 15) and a handful in recipes. `px` literals in recipes: orin 21, twx 28, foundations 12, mostly `1px` borders and `2px` outlines. These need border-width and outline tokens. |
| No width/height media queries | None in source or generated CSS. Container queries: 67 / 94 / 105 in the three apps' CSS. |
| Logical properties only | Generated CSS still has physical declarations: Orin 10, techworx 47. The code block's gutter and copy button use `text-align: right` and `border-left/right`; source files in `cv-kit` (25) and `twx` (14) use physical names. |
| Hover inside `(hover: hover)` | Held: the hover rules are in the media query. |
| Layers | Held: `reset, base, tokens, recipes, utilities`. The reason `!important` was ever tempting was a base-layer rule fighting a recipe; put state in the recipe. |
| Never author `any` or `unknown` | One match in `packages/components`. |

Panda is set to `strictTokens: true`. `strictPropertyValues` and `validation` are not set. `staticCss: { recipes: '*' }` emits every recipe: the generated CSS is 157 KB (docs), 214 KB (Orin) and 271 KB (techworx) before compression.

## Foundation (`packages/foundations`, `packages/components`)

- **Brand branching inside shared code.** 13 `brand === 'orin' | 'twx'` branches in `frame.ts` (4), `index.ts` (8) and `typography.ts` (1). The nav sheet, the rail thresholds and the `chapterSheet` condition each added a branch. These should be brand data (tokens or variables) read by brand-free code.
- **`frame.ts` and `siteNavParts.ts` are shared edit points** with the techworx work; every change needs hunk-level staging. Splitting Orin's staged reading template from techworx's single-rail template into their own modules would stop that.
- **`MenuSheet`**: see headline 2. It also duplicates link markup that `SiteNav.astro` writes again.
- **`useThemeChoice`**: now an external-store hook (`useSyncExternalStore`), pending state for `null`. Good shape; it is the model for the others.
- **`stack-layout`** is an Astro-only wrapper; there is no React `Stack`.
- **Tests that pin thresholds**: `index.test.ts` and the CSS tests assert exact container widths. They need to assert behaviour (which rail is open at which width) from the tokens.
- **No tests**: `action-content`, `button-types`, `code-highlight`, `copy-text`, `footer`, `stack-layout` (components).

## Orin wrapper (`packages/orin`)

- Components without tests: `button-link`, `hero`, `lattice`, `lockup`, `margin-note`, `page-intro`, `table`, `tool-hero`.
- Raw anchors where `Link` should be: `hero-card`, `tile-card`.
- `recipes.ts` holds six unrelated recipes in one file (button, chip, section label, search field, command line, code block) next to folder-per-component recipes: pick one layout.
- `page-intro` takes its lattice span through an inline `style`; it should be a recipe slot.
- `view-toggle` is the second copy of the three-way control (see below).

## techworx wrapper (`packages/twx`)

- Duplicates eight Orin component names (see headline 3).
- Components without tests: `article`, `button-link`, `field`, `work-index`.
- Raw anchors in `work-row`, `post-row` and `work-card`.
- `apps/techworx` carries 12 `css()` files, 54 hex values in one data file and 47 physical declarations in its CSS.
- Another session is changing this layer now; anything here is coordinated first.

## Sites

- `apps/orin-dx`: 68 source files, 3 tests. The brand-page specimens (`swatch-grid`, `ladder-rows`, `state-matrix` and others) are real components with real state and no tests.
- `apps/orin-dx-docs`: 12 `css()` calls in 6 files.
- `packages/cv-kit`: no tests, 25 physical declarations. The CV layout is locked; only its edges align to the grid.

## Proposed component set

Base components own behaviour and accessibility, take tokens only, and carry brand differences as recipe variants. Instances compose them with state and content.

| Layer | Component | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Layout | `Stack`, `Cluster` | Own the gap between siblings by spacing token (`tight`, `normal`, `loose`); wrap by container query. Replaces per-element margins. |
| Layout | `ButtonGroup` | Spaced or attached, horizontal or vertical, wraps by container. Composes `Button`. |
| Base | `Link` | One `<a>`: current state, external handling, focus ring, target size. Variants `inline`, `nav`, `quiet`, `icon`. |
| Base | `Button` | One component; Orin and techworx are skins. |
| Base | `SegmentedControl` | Pending frame for an unknown value; the pill and its slide live here. |
| Base | `Sheet` | Dialog, scrim, inert, focus cycle, full-screen and dropdown placements. |
| Base | `Disclosure` | Dropdowns and the breadcrumb switcher. |
| Instance | `HorizontalNav` | `Link` (`nav`) list; collapses by container. |
| Instance | `BrandLink` | `Link` plus mark and wordmark. |
| Instance | `EmailLink`, `GitHubLink` | `Link` plus icon, data from one shared `contacts` module. |
| Instance | `LinkGroup` | Heading plus a vertical `Link` list. |
| Instance | `ThemeToggle` | `SegmentedControl` plus `useThemeChoice` plus icons and labels. Replaces five copies. |
| Instance | `NavSheet`, `SiteNav`, `SiteFooter` | Compositions of the above. |

## Order of work

1. **Reconcile the specs.** Decide SPEC-003c against what shipped (props or DOM read, sub-chapters, the 1280px or 768px rail) and amend SPEC-001, SPEC-003a and PLAN-004. No new component work before this.
2. **Port the rules checker** and add the new rules (no `!important`, no inline style literals, no `css()` in components, no raw colour or `px`, no width media queries, logical properties only, no raw `<a>` outside `Link`). Run it on the generated CSS and on source. Put the Playwright suites in CI.
3. **Specs for the base set**, then `Link`, `Button`, `Stack`/`Cluster`/`ButtonGroup`, `SegmentedControl`, `Sheet`, in that order, each with tests and an API entry.
4. **Collapse the duplicates** (`ThemeToggle`, `Button`, `CodeBlock`, `CommandLine`, `MarginNote`) onto the base components, Orin first, techworx with that session's agreement.
5. **Move the app components** that are really design-system components into the packages; convert `css()` calls to recipes.
6. **Clean the debt**: border-width and outline tokens, logical properties, `strictPropertyValues`, the one-recipe-per-folder layout, brand branches turned into data.

# Accessibility: the manual pass

The automated audit (`apps/site-e2e/e2e/a11y-audit.spec.ts`, run by `just e2e-sites`) checks every built page of techworx.dev, orin-dx.com and the docs for: WCAG 2.2 AA through axe in both themes, real target sizes with a mouse and on a phone, forced colours (focus outlines, icons, selected states), 3:1 field borders, Tab order and focus the nav never hides, reflow at 320px, text spacing, and headings and landmarks.

Automated checks find roughly a third to a half of accessibility problems. This pass covers the rest. It takes about two hours across both sites. Record each finding with the page, the device and assistive technology, what happened and what should have happened.

## Before you start

- Build the sites (`just build`) and serve them (`just preview techworx`, `just preview orin-dx`), or use a deploy preview.
- Pages to cover on each site: home, one case study or tool page, the brand page, the CV (techworx), the tools index and principles (Orin), and the 404.

## 1. Screen readers

Run each task with VoiceOver on macOS Safari, VoiceOver on an iPhone, and TalkBack on an Android phone with Chrome.

- [ ] The page title is announced on load and says which page this is.
- [ ] The headings list (VoiceOver rotor, TalkBack headings) reads as an outline of the page: one h1, then sections in order, with no empty or duplicate headings.
- [ ] The landmarks list has one banner, one main, the site navigation and, on long pages, the chapter list, each with a name that says what it is.
- [ ] "Skip to main content" works and lands before the page's h1. (Known issue: on pages built on the document template, the h1 sits in the lead outside main. See the audit findings.)
- [ ] Every link and button says where it goes or what it does out of context: no "click here", and no icon-only control without a name.
- [ ] The current page in the nav is announced as current.
- [ ] The theme switch announces its options and which one is selected, and announces the change.
- [ ] The phone menu announces that it opened, keeps the screen reader inside it while open, and returns to the Menu button when closed.
- [ ] Figures and artwork: informative images have alt text that says what the image shows and why it is there; decorative ones (dots, strands, lattice) are skipped.
- [ ] Tables are read with their headers, and a wide table in a scroll region can be reached and scrolled.
- [ ] Disclosures ("3 sources", reference sections) announce expanded or collapsed, and their content is only reachable when open.
- [ ] Copy buttons announce that the command was copied.
- [ ] The CV reads in a sensible order: name, role, contact, summary, stats, then experience.

## 2. Keyboard only

Use Chrome and Safari on macOS. In Safari, turn on Settings > Advanced > "Press Tab to highlight each item on a webpage" first.

- [ ] Every task can be done without a mouse: reach every link and control, open and close the menu and the breadcrumb switcher, switch theme, filter the work index, open each disclosure, use each figure's light and dark switch.
- [ ] The focus ring is visible on every stop, on every surface, in both themes.
- [ ] Escape closes any open menu, sheet or popover, and focus returns to what opened it.
- [ ] Arrow keys move within grouped controls (the theme switch, segmented controls) and Tab moves past the group.
- [ ] Nothing traps focus, and nothing takes focus unexpectedly on load or after a change.

# Test pruning plan: behaviour versus visual

Policy (owner, 2026-10-13): we test the behaviour of components and helpers, not CSS or colour. Visual testing comes later.

All counts come from the final audit, which counted test definitions by script. The per-area classification reports disagree with its visual/borderline split in places (see "Reconciliation"). Files with a disagreement need a per-file check before any deletion.

## 1. Totals

| Area                     | Files   | Tests    | Behaviour       | Visual          | Borderline      |
| ------------------------ | ------- | -------- | --------------- | --------------- | --------------- |
| foundations src (non-ui) | 11      | 77       | 22 (28.6%)      | 38 (49.4%)      | 17 (22.1%)      |
| foundations ui           | 16      | 135      | 86 (63.7%)      | 46 (34.1%)      | 3 (2.2%)        |
| components               | 30      | 282      | 167 (59.2%)     | 96 (34.0%)      | 19 (6.7%)       |
| orin                     | 20      | 101      | 62 (61.4%)      | 35 (34.7%)      | 4 (4.0%)        |
| twx                      | 30      | 76       | 46 (60.5%)      | 25 (32.9%)      | 5 (6.6%)        |
| apps unit                | 12      | 56       | 36 (64.3%)      | 11 (19.6%)      | 9 (16.1%)       |
| nav-fixture e2e          | 31      | 287      | 129 (44.9%)     | 100 (34.8%)     | 58 (20.2%)      |
| site-e2e                 | 16      | 102      | 54 (52.9%)      | 33 (32.4%)      | 15 (14.7%)      |
| **Overall**              | **166** | **1116** | **602 (53.9%)** | **384 (34.4%)** | **130 (11.6%)** |

98 of the 166 files are behaviour-only. `packages/cv-kit` and `packages/rules` have no tests, and `apps/orin-dx-docs` has none either.

### Reconciliation

| Area               | Area report (tests: B / V / Bd) | Audit (B / V / Bd)      |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| foundations non-ui | 77: 19 / 42 / 16                | 22 / 38 / 17            |
| foundations ui     | 139: 91 / 46 / 3                | 86 / 46 / 3 (135 tests) |
| components         | 282: 167 / 93 / 22              | 167 / 96 / 19           |
| orin + twx         | 177: 110 / 54 / 13              | 108 / 60 / 9            |
| apps unit          | 56: 36 / 14 / 6                 | 36 / 11 / 9             |
| nav-fixture e2e    | 287: 112 / 114 / 61             | 129 / 100 / 58          |
| site-e2e           | 102: 59 / 33 / 10               | 54 / 33 / 15            |

The audit's orin + twx figures are the sums of its orin (62 / 35 / 4) and twx (46 / 25 / 5) rows.

Disputed files:

- `fieldBox.test.ts` and `tokenUsage.test.ts` are on the audit's behaviour-only list, but the area reports class them as visual. I treat `fieldBox` as visual, and `tokenUsage` as an owner decision (lint).
- `prehydration.spec.ts` is behaviour/borderline in the audit but visual in the area report.
- `widths.spec.ts` L129 (visual order equals DOM order) is behaviour in the audit but visual in the area report.

## 2. Ten files with the most visual tests

These ten files hold 184 of the 384 visual tests (47.9%).

| #   | File                                                         | Visual | Of total |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------ | -------- |
| 1   | `packages/components/src/site-nav-css.test.ts`               | 28     | 33       |
| 2   | `packages/orin/src/recipeCss.test.ts`                        | 25     | 28       |
| 3   | `
# Deferred accessibility and visual tests, 2026-10-13

Tests removed in the pruning of 2026-10-13 because they measure appearance or an accessibility contract (forced colours, 44px targets, reflow, print layout, contrast re-measurements, reduced-motion CSS copies). They are recoverable from git history (the pruning commits of that day). When visual and accessibility testing is taken up, this is the checklist of what to rebuild as one deliberate suite, not per recipe.

## 2A foundations non-ui

- primary.test.ts: text.onPrimary reads on %s at 4.5:1 in both themes (contrast re-measurement, outside contrast.test.ts)
- index.test.ts: %s on %s (%s) reaches 4.5:1 (text on grounds contrast re-measurement, outside contrast.test.ts)
- index.test.ts: hover only applies where the pointer can hover (hover-only-under-hover:hover copy)
- sheet/sheet.test.ts: rows and the close control are 44px targets; the close icon is 24px (44px target)
- sheet/sheet.test.ts: the close control: a colour transition only under no-preference, and a pressed ::before 4px inside (reduced-motion CSS copy)

## 2B foundations ui

- packages/foundations/src/ui/sheet/sheet.test.tsx: the popup scrolls focus to rest below a header of the same least block size (scroll-padding under sticky header; plan 3b: later browser test that a focused element is not hidden under the sheet header)
- packages/foundations/src/ui/sheet/sheet.test.tsx: is opaque under forced colours
- packages/foundations/src/ui/link/linkNav.test.tsx: under forced colours every link has a transparent block-end border, the current one CanvasText, and no pill
- packages/foundations/src/ui/link/linkNav.test.tsx: hover changes the colour alone and only where a pointer can hover
- packages/foundations/src/ui/sheet/sheetLayer.test.tsx: reduced motion has no starting offset (every transform or opacity the sheet sets from data-motion is inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)
- packages/foundations/src/ui/sheet/sheetLayer.test.tsx: the default popup declares %s in recipes.defaults (plan 3b: later real-browser test that a consumer class overrides the default popup)

## 2C components (packages/components/src)

- site-nav-css.test.ts: the logo is capped at 64px and its link is a 44px target (AC-112)
- site-nav-css.test.ts: prefers-contrast: more makes the bar solid with a control-strength edge, light/dark (AC-121)
- site-nav-css.test.ts: reduced transparency and missing backdrop-filter support give the solid bar (AC-070)
- site-nav-css.t

content.content:
== b8faa0a5
Meet the accessibility audit on orin-dx.com and the shared nav
The site nav's logo link and Orin's copy button reach 44px on touch. Every Orin control is 32px tall on any pointer: the theme switch and the small segmented control reach it with a hit area above and below, never sideways, and the loop demo's buttons and the sources disclosure grow to it. Small text that took a ramp colour (the ledger's rail numerals, the loop's stage labels) takes ink for 4.5:1; the ramp stays on nodes, rules and large numerals. The Orin case study states the theme switch's width exception, as techworx's does. The audit skips content inside a closed disclosure, which is never painted, and records the theme switch's exception for every site. The token check treats figures o


== 1d61cb60
Give the techworx brand page one banner and keep the CV's toolbar inside main
The brand opener was a <header> outside <main>, which made it a second banner landmark beside the site nav; it is a plain block now. The CV's toolbar (the date and the print hint) sat outside every landmark; main now holds the toolbar and the sheet, and the sheet keeps its classes, so nothing moves on screen or on paper.


== a04ddca3
Fix the card strands' fades, which the token conversion had broken
Converting the mask gradients to spacing tokens left bare parentheses where CSS needs calc(), so the browser dropped the masks. The three drawings then met in hard cuts 96px in from each end, which showed up at phone width, where a card is barely wider than its two corner caps. The gradients are valid again and the pieces fade into each other.


== 05844c28
Fix the Orin brand page's glass opacity and both-rails width
The nav glass percentage printed NaN because the colour was a token reference sliced as if it were hex, and the non-empty fallback never applied. It now reads the nav-ground colour's alpha (92%), with a test. The page also said both rails open at 1104px, the width of the footer's rail condition; it now reads the both-rails condition (1304px). The frame state conditions are typed by name so the page can read them.


== 0a9018ca
Give Tools and Principles the home hero's ribbon and fix the family cards, marks and ledger
Tools and Principles now use the home hero's ribbon route and width, with the text kept in a column that ends where the strands begin, the ribbon quieter so text over it stays easy to read, and enough height that the next section starts below it. The brand page gets the on-load ignite back, since the mark lives there now: the mark lights and the lattice spreads from it once, and reduced motion skips it. The brand plates stack one per row.

The tool marks in the family, loop and off-loop cards were being drawn 32 wide by 36 tall from a square source, which stretched them and put them 2px low in their boxes; they now sit at the badge's own mark size and centre. Tool names in the family cards drop to the lede size, a hovered row measures its padding to the letters so it is even above and below, and the legend sits a paragraph gap under the cards. On Principles the claim braces stay inline and the loop diagram's outline stays inside the content column instead of pushing past it.


== e23aae76
Put every control on the 32/40/48 scale, grow touch targets to 44 and make focus rings follow the shape
Orin buttons are 32 and 40 (they were 30 and 42), a size never shrinks on touch (Tabs lg), and on a coarse pointer site buttons, rail rows, filters and footer links reach 44. Checkbox, radio, switch and the site icon buttons get an invisible hit area, 24 on any pointer and 44 on touch, with no layout change. Rings follow the visible shape: links, ghost buttons and buttons share the control radius, Orin nav rings sit on the pill, segmented and view-toggle cells take the track's inner radius, the checkbox is 4 and the techworx radio gets the canvas gap. The case-study gap is 48 and the chapter rail's top padding 32, so the first figure stays level with the rail's first row. The wordmark keeps 


== cdb331d7
Put the mark at the side on a phone and refocus Principles' "what you get" on what Orin DX brings
On a phone the brand and tool marks led the opener on a row of their own, which left an empty band and a large lattice around a small mark. The mark is now 112px at the top right, level with the kicker, the title is narrowed to clear it and the lede runs full width under it.

The "what you get" section of Principles listed each tool's stage, which is not a principle and is on each tool's own page. It now says what the whole thing brings, why it is different (the three positions already on the page) and how each tool helps, in the tool data's own one-line summaries. The new wording is logged for review.


== c77778b1
Make 760px the first wide width everywhere, as SPEC-013 already says
SPEC-013 AC-004 and AC-021 put the collapse threshold on the wide side (760px wide, 759px narrow), but the width conditions, the sheet's closeWhen, the breadcrumbs measure and the nav-fixture tests had kept 760px narrow, with the frame thresholds parked at 761px to match. They now follow the spec: the nav, compact, chapterSheet and breadcrumbs conditions are exact complements at compactAt, and frame-breakout-at and frame-left-rail-at are 760px in both brands. That removes the 8px band where the nav was a link row but the chapter list was not yet a rail, and it makes the tablet step agree with every width condition, so the remaining compact call sites can move to it with no boundary change. S


== d72d7458
Draw the open base-layer decisions: brass depth, focus ring side, sheet height and corners, group stacking, subsections, island failure
A drawing page only (ui-examples-open). The phones are CSS mocks drawn with the real surface, radius and shadow roles because the Sheet prototype does not have these rules yet; the buttons, toggles and choice controls are the real components.

Written 13 Oct 2026 after two decisions turned out to be recorded but not applied. Every owner decision in `design-decisions-2026-10-13.md` (and the ones recorded elsewhere) is listed with what the code does today. "Done" means it is in the code and a check passed. "Not checked" means I did not look. Update this file in the same commit as any change that touches a decision.

## Status key

- **Done**: in the code and verified.
- **Partial**: some of it is in the code; the rest is named.
- **Not done**: recorded, not applied.
- **Waiting**: needs an answer from the owner before it can be applied.

# D-outcomes: quality of outcomes, ~/projects/pages (+ orin-dx-site)

Scope notes: ~/projects/orin-dx-site holds only brand/ (HTML artifacts, .bak files, no git, no docs/). All the named docs (review-2026-10-03, review-2026-10-11-foundation-and-wrappers, ship-readiness, design-system-coverage, design-system-integration-audit, system-deltas, codex-handoff) live in ~/projects/pages/docs/. 538 commits, 30 Sep-16 Oct 2026; 479 carry a Claude-Session trailer, 460 an Entire-Checkpoint.

## What came through Wisp plugins vs ad hoc
- Plugin-driven (spec/plan/gate pipeline): SPEC-001..013 in docs/specs (JSON spec@1 + verdict files), PLAN-001/003/004/005 + challenger files in docs/plans, SPEC-002 rules checker. Verdicts are verdict@1-style (artifact_type spec@1, retry_count, blockers).
- Ad hoc / exploratory: everything after 13 Oct. Strands, landing, Tools/Principles, brand-page rebuild (SPEC-014/015/016, 14 Oct, ~110 commits) shipped without gate. Commit 0ea8be77: "drafted ... before the work moved to an exploratory build. They are not approved scope." SPEC-015-audit.json is an overall:fail that was never resolved. The 16 Oct a11y audit, case-study rewrite, copy reviews, ship-readiness are ad hoc.
- Design-system "base layer" docs (design-system-rules/coverage/api, proposals/*) are owner+Claude prose, not plugin artifacts, but SPEC-005..012 derive from them.

## Defects found late (after specs/gates passed) and who found them
1. Specs and code had drifted (review-2026-10-11 headline 1): nav sheet and rails shipped without reconciling SPEC-001/003a/003c/PLAN-004 (props vs DOM read, 768 vs 1280 rail). Found by a human-directed review, not by drift-checker. Later fixed by rewriting: SPEC-013 (ef3dcf26) replaced parts of SPEC-001/003c.
2. 760px boundary (c77778b1, 13 Oct): code kept 760 narrow with frame thresholds parked at 761 while SPEC-013 AC-004/021 said 760 wide; created an 8px band where nav was a link row but chapters were not a rail. Spec said it; implementation and its 296 nav-fixture tests pinned the wrong value. Tests asserted the same wrong constant.
3. Brand page showed "NaN%" glass opacity and wrong both-rails width (1104 vs 1304), 05844c28 / ship-readiness. A shipped, visible defect on a page about the design system; only a crawl for "NaN" caught it.
4. Card strand fades broken by a token conversion: bare parentheses instead of calc(), browser dropped masks, hard cuts visible at phone width (a04ddca3). No visual test existed; deleted 12 Oct.
5. Strand marks drawn stretched 32x36 from a square source and 2px low; family/loop cards, phone opener with empty band (0a9018ca, cdb331d7). Visual/layout/responsive, found by human review.
6. Focus: rings clipped or on wrong shape/side (bf6b44d6, a0af8700, ef5cc2a7, 88490112, ad42137f, e23aae76); focus not returned after sheet close (12d82f79, 98ae9acc); focus ring colour changed to blue because it clashed with text/borders (2c81bd88). Many are owner-driven design decisions rather than plain bugs, but SPEC-001/005/007 had formally "passed" focus criteria first.
7. Controls/touch targets: 32/40/48 scale and 44px touch (e23aae76) retrofitted 13 Oct; then 16 Oct audit still found: colour-card labels at 2.9-4.3:1 (opacity 0.7), CV contact icons overlapping, work filters 43px wide (ab5a7e4a), Orin controls under 44, small text on ramp colours below 4.5:1 (b8faa0a5), two banner landmarks on techworx brand page and CV toolbar outside main (1d61cb60), h1 outside main on document-template pages (known issue in docs/plans/accessibility-manual-pass.md). Contrast and target size were found by the first real automated suite, 4 days after the base specs "all passed".
8. Review 3 Oct (review-2026-10-03.md) worklist: Blocker/High items that code review found only after build: nav toggle labelled Preview/Outline with Cmd+Y flipping theme (F1); logo cap regression AC-112/113/017 caught only by the manual baseline `just e2e` (4 failures); CV print .cvpage.cvpage.cvpage with 67 !important and 40 hex (F3); --radius-md removed so corners square (F4); PostRow gap 5 emitted 5px not 24px (F5); hero padding emitted 96px (F6); Orin Button 14/400 not 16/600; TileGrid 2 cols on phones with lone cards. Token-key mistakes "already did twice" (two numbering schemes). Most are still "pending verification", not verified-fixed.
9. Copy: case studies contain misattributions (case-study-audit-2026-10-15: H1 wrong image as Chosen, H2 "88% I chose" contradicted by transcript, H4 AI research credited to owner); "two views" stale copy; claims dropped from hero (BRA-7). No spec criterion covers truthfulness; only human/model fact-check caught them. Docs link to docs.orin-dx.com pointed to an empty site.
10. SEO/meta: ship-readiness crawl is the only check; docs stub has no description/lang; /writing/ builds "0 posts" and is unlinked. A seo-geo worktree exists but no spec.

## Why gates did not catch these
- Gates judge the spec on its own terms (internal consistency). Verdict blockers are about contradictions between ACs, missing states, wording ("AC-044 label role holds only for techworx"). That is valuable: SPEC-001 needed 13 verdict files, SPEC-005 retry_count 6, SPEC-002b hit the 3-retry escalation. But it found zero rendered-outcome defects; no step renders anything.
- Specs are testable-by-construction but over-specified at the wrong level: SPEC-013 has 39 ACs each of paragraph length with exact px, route-interception recipes and "Replaces SPEC-001 AC-056" chains; SPEC-001 had 120+ ACs. They read as CSS assertions (e.g. "logo capped 64px", "column gap 8px", duration before data-ready). The owner then decided on 12-13 Oct that visual/CSS-pin tests are not wanted: testing-prune-plan.md deleted 384 of 1116 tests (34%), including 28/33 in site-nav-css.test.ts, because they pinned values not behaviour. So a large share of what muse specs demanded (and smith/plan tasks implemented) was brittle CSS mirroring, then discarded. Meanwhile real visual risks (contrast, reflow, forced colours, target size) were parked in deferred-accessibility-tests.md and only rebuilt as one suite on 16 Oct (9dfe58e4, e9d921e9), which immediately found real failures.
- Spec/design thrash: SPEC-004..012 were gated pass on 11 Oct then "revised for design decisions" in one batch on 12 Oct (6fb08ba3, f8896db5, 1faebc1c). Visual decisions (focus ring side, brass depth, frosted ground, sheet corners) were made after gating via drawn pages (d72d7458, "ui-examples-open"). Muse specs encoded states and ARIA but not the owner's visual intent, which had to be discovered by looking.
- Gates passed first time (retry 0) for SPEC-006..012 on 11 Oct; they were produced in one day (8 specs). Suggests either good drafts or low adversarial pressure; each was immediately revised the next day for 5+ owner decisions.

## Verification infrastructure
- Exists: Vitest (~1100 tests before pruning, AC-id references in ~100 test files, e.g. apps/site-e2e/e2e/nav-sheet.spec.ts), nav-fixture Playwright suite (296 passing; Firefox absent), site-e2e (19 spec files, real built sites), Storybook (apps/storybook/stories; "about one line per component", SiteNav no story at 3 Oct), axe in six Vitest files and the 16 Oct audit.
- Tied to spec criteria: nav/chapter/breadcrumb specs reference AC ids; the later strands/landing work (SPEC-014..016) has none; the 16 Oct audit is tied to WCAG success criteria, not spec ACs.
- Gaps: Playwright suites are `runInCI: false` / "manual; not part of ci" (justfile lines 60-66; review-2026-10-11 headline 5; review-2026-10-03 testing gaps). Zero toHaveScreenshot / no screenshot regression (grep: 0), no Storybook build/visual in CI, no JS size budget (271 KB hydrated), packages/rules is a README only (SPEC-002 rules checker never ported). The enforcement that review 11 Oct says is missing is exactly the layer that would have caught NaN, calc() breakage, hex/px/!important.
- Owner policy 13 Oct: "we test behaviour, visual testing comes later" - correct for brittleness, but nothing replaced it until 16 Oct.

## Spec-code drift, duplicates, competing abstractions
- Drift: SPEC-001/003a/003c vs shipped (above); decisions-status.md (13 Oct) opens "after two decisions turned out to be recorded but not applied". design-system-coverage lists MenuSheet "removed; NavSheet built" while review 11 Oct still describes MenuSheet; docs go stale within a day (commits "Correct stale thresholds ... in the docs", 8cebb61b "four stale tests").
- Duplicates (review 11 Oct, still visible): packages/orin and packages/twx both have button, button-link, code-block, command-line, hero, icon, margin-note, view-toggle. packages/foundations/src/ui AND packages/components/src both carry button, button-link, field, sheet-ish components (23 app files import foundations/ui). Five theme-toggle copies were the stated target. 40 files in apps/orin-dx and techworx still call css() (policy: recipes only). Brand branching (13 `brand === ...`) inside shared code.
- Spec numbering collisions in practice: SPEC-002/002a/b/c split, SPEC-003/a/b/c, PLAN-003 vs PLAN-004 superseded; "Replaces SPEC-001 AC-xxx" chains make the live contract hard to read.

## Overall judgement
Plugin work reliably produced consistent, testable, well-challenged spec text and plans for interaction/ARIA/geometry of components (nav, rails, base layer). It did not produce good visual outcomes by itself: every visible-quality defect above (NaN, broken masks, stretched marks, phone openers, contrast/targets, landmarks, copy truth) was found by a human look, a post-hoc audit or a new test suite, and the best-defended area (nav) is also where the owner deleted the most tests as too brittle. The late, strong results came from two ad hoc moves: a whole-site crawl/axe/target-size/reflow audit (16 Oct) and independent fact-check/review docs. The missing pipeline stage is a rendered-outcome check (screenshots at 320/375/760/1440 in both themes and brands, contrast/target/reflow probe, copy-vs-source check) run in CI and referenced from spec criteria.
